subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Correction and reflection: rehearsal and performance
essential_question: How can understanding music composition, production, and performance help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for rehearsal and performance, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of rehearsal and performance.
Check, revise, or improve work about rehearsal and performance using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about rehearsal and performance.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Critique and reflection work on rehearsal and performance. Critique and reflection: organize events, marks, sounds, words, objects, or movements through rehearsal and performance, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Anticipate one likely weak point and check it without surrendering the artistic decision.
primary_task: Target for this correct session: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for rehearsal and performance, then demonstrate corrected understanding. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of rehearsal and performance. Check, revise, or improve work about rehearsal and performance using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about rehearsal and performance; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. 1. Error analysis: Name the observable mismatch in earlier work without judging taste or effort. Locate it, compare it with the stated criterion, and choose the smallest useful repair. 2. Supported revision: Test the repair on a separate small study before changing the scored work. Use a different cue or representation and record what the test reveals. 3. Fresh transfer: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan. Record what the fresh evidence shows; keep the earlier attempt without penalty. Your choices remain yours: Different medium, subject or source material, sequence, criterion to test, final revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about rehearsal and performance, and it belongs to "Music Composition, Production, and Performance", which also covers separate topics such as rhythm harmony and melody. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about rehearsal and performance; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.

deliverable: Error analysis, Supported revision, Fresh transfer, with the observable Arts evidence and learner-owned decisions identified in each block.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the alternate explanation, supported attempt, and new transfer; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres an aural element (rehearsal and performance). Provide a fully equivalent non-aural route: notated, written, or graphic representation; visual or tactile pulse (a moving marker, a tapped or felt beat); and vibration or sight-reading in place of listening. Do not require the learner to hear a pitch, interval, or timbre to demonstrate understanding of it.

Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting rehearsal and performance.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce rehearsal and performance to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one sequence relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact sequence evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply rehearsal and performance under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on rehearsal and performance rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one sequence relationship while working on rehearsal and performance.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.

age_policy.language: Direct middle-school arts language with established vocabulary and explicit checkpoints.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

concept_instruction.title: What rehearsal and performance means here
concept_instruction.body: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: Moving between media can reveal structure but may change the measured skill; name which evidence transfers and which does not. Worked example: Short → short-short → long can be drawn, tapped, moved, or silently counted while preserving its pattern of arrival, urgency, and rest. Non-example: Switching media and changing every relationship at once makes it impossible to tell what caused the new effect.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in rehearsal and performance.
technique_sequence.why: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for rehearsal and performance is present, but the record does not yet locate sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
